analysis: The first half of this stretch was genuinely gorgeous — you hit 8h 5m on the third night with nearly 50 minutes of deep sleep and REM pushing close to two hours, which is your body doing exactly what it's supposed to do when you actually let it. Then something shifted around the middle of the week and you've been sitting in the sixes and low sevens since, with that one 6h 30m night being the obvious dip. Your REM has stayed impressively consistent across the whole seven nights — hovering between 1h 33m and 1h 48m almost every single night, which tells me the wind-down stack is doing real work even when total sleep drops. The gap right now is duration, not architecture, so the question is what changed after that 8h 5m peak — because your sleep clearly knows how to be good, it just needs you to keep showing up for bedtime like it's a date you actually want to keep.
